title.narrative: Green Skills– climate adapted TVET and strengthen socio-economic resilience of youth for sustainable future in Pakistan

description.narrative: Overall objective: Green skills in the vocational training systems of the provinces of KP, Punjab and Sindh contribute to SDG 13) and SDG 8), which particularly benefit young people.Project objective: 2,700 young people in the target areas in KP, Punjab and Sindh have improved economic independence through the application of technical and vocational green skills in workplaces and businesses, promoted by local actors in the vocational training system, in particular 15 training institutes and 90 supporting community organizations.

Pakistan faces economic and climate challenges that necessitate a shift toward a green economy, requiring a workforce equipped with green skills. This project enhances civil society engagement and youth resilience by supporting and adopting green skills into the TVET system and supporting climate adaptation and mitigation. It focuses on four key areas: strengthening TVET institutions by improving faculty expertise, infrastructure, and coordination; increasing youth awareness, access, and completion of green TVET programs while enhancing employment opportunities; building CSOs’ capacity to promote green TVET, support enrollment, and influence policy; and strengthening SABAWON, LPP, and RDF for effective project delivery.

The main direct target group consist of 3000 vulnerable youth (age 18 – 29 years); 50% men and 50% women, including at least 2% People with Disabilities (PWDs) and at least 2% members of ethnic and religious minorities of both genders, who will receive green technical and vocational skills preparing them for employed and self-employed income generation and supporting an increased awareness on climate change adaptation and mitigation. The target group is planned to be split equally over the three target areas Peshawar Division in KP, Bahawalpur, Multan and Lodhrans divisions in Punjab and Bhambore and Hyderabad divisions in Sindh (each 1000 youth). 90 CBOs/CSOs, registered with the Social Welfare departments or Charity Commission. These small-scale grassroot organizations play a key role in promoting green skill TVET among targeted youth and their communities.15 public training institutes (five per province) will offer green skill training courses to the targeted youth.Local Partner Organizations: SABAWON, RDF and LPP are implementing the project in their target regions and benefit from technical and institutional capacity building relevant to effectively realize project objectives.
